description: Routine easy run for a marathon runner. Response must open with a specific metric or observation — never with praise or any affirmation phrase. Tests the core 'start with the observation' behavior.

ground_truth.notes: OPENER TEST: Alex ran a routine easy 7.2mi at 9:05/mi with HR 141. The response MUST open with a specific metric or observation — e.g. 'HR held at 141 — solidly aerobic for 7 miles' or '7.2 miles at 9:05/mi — HR stayed at 141 the whole way.' PASSING opener: first word/phrase is a number, data point, or named metric ('7.2 miles...', 'HR held at 141...', 'Zone 2 HR...'). FAILING opener: first word is a praise/affirmation word with no data ('Great run', 'Nice work', 'Solid effort', 'That's a solid easy day'). Note: 'solidly in Zone 2' or 'exactly in Zone 2' AFTER a number is acceptable — the qualifier is modifying the metric, not serving as an opener. Score below 7 only if the message opens with pure praise before any data point. Miles logged this week is 18.2mi (7.2 today + 6.0 Wednesday + 5.0 Monday — authoritative figure).
